title: The Raccoon Problem
paragraphs: “Motoyasu-sama just doesn’t remember the unnecessary stuff! In fact, he’s teaching us some elegant choreography!”
“Yay!”
“Is this how it goes?”

Yuki-chan and the others recently danced behind me, performing the Idol dance moves I’ve been teaching them. They danced exactly as I’d shown them, and everyone’s eyes were glued to them. Even Father, who had looked exasperated, is now a little impressed by the high quality of everyone’s dancing.
“I’ve gone off on a tangent. We were talking about what caused Wild Ofumi to be troubled.”
“Come to think of it, Gaelion-chan did meet the version of me from the first world that Motoyasu-kun knows, didn’t she?”
“That’s right. Compared to the current Naofumi, he was wild—so he was ‘Wild Naofumi.’”
When Rival said that, Father’s spirits dropped. Did something happen?
“Ah… that’s the me who used to talk about ‘resources’ like a thief.”
“That’s right. The thief I took under my wing eventually made a name for himself as a Robin Hood-type, so you don’t need to worry about it too much.”
“I’m not so sure about that.”

“The issues with my family back home got resolved, and the Robin Hood-type thief didn’t seem to mind it all that much either. Since he’s the same Naofumi, I’d appreciate it if you didn’t think badly of him. Oh, I’ve gone off on a tangent again.”
“S-sorry.”
You’re constantly derailing the conversation and causing trouble for Father! Serves you right!
“It’s fine, really. It makes me happy to be able to talk with Naofumi.”
“Gaelion-chan is such a nice person… I mean, dragon, right?”
Oh? That strange atmosphere from earlier is creeping back in.
“I’m glad to hear you say that.”
Rival doesn’t seem particularly bothered by it. Is work that busy for him? Well, I’m swamped preparing for the Idol activities of Filolial-sama and the others, too.

“To summarize it briefly, he was the right-hand man of Wild Ofumi, and it seems he was troubled because the original Raph and his kind were thought to be the same species as the Demi-Humans causing problems in this area.”
“So that means the right-hand man of the Shield Hero, whom the Spear Hero worships, is a Raccoon…”

The panda says this with a sigh. What’s going on here? Are you guys dissing the Older Sister? If you do that, she’ll crush you all. Who knows how many times I’ve been blown away during these loops? We absolutely mustn’t anger the Older Sister from the first world.
“The fact that they ultimately led the world to peace… well, you really managed to find a serious Raccoon-type, didn’t you?”
“Raccoon race?”

“Ah, the Raccoon race—among the Demi-Human races, their physical abilities are average, I suppose, but their reputation is pretty bad because of the infamy of that region in Shieldfreeden. They’re on the quiet side as children, but once they grow up, they tend to become hot-tempered and lazy. Since they aren’t exactly good-looking either, the overall reputation of the species isn’t great.”

You really know your way around races, Panda. However, I had no idea Big Sister’s race had such a bad reputation. She’s very serious and hardworking. She seems to devote herself to training whenever she finds a spare moment—she has the character befitting someone who walks beside Father.
“To be precise, the raccoon who served as Naofumi’s right-hand man belongs to a closely related species of raccoon, so a monster like Gaelion could tell at a glance that it’s different.”
“Oh, really?”

“To begin with, the raccoon in question is a particularly distinct subspecies even within the broader ‘raccoon’ category. It’s different from the main raccoon species, but it’s still generally treated as a raccoon.”

I don’t quite understand. But since there are so many different types of Filolial-sama, I can see why there might be variations within Big Sister’s species, the raccoons. In short, it’s probably like the Raccoon-type Shieldfreeden.

“So they’re a race that looks similar but is actually different? Come to think of it… there are quite a few cases where species are initially thought to be the same but turn out to be different upon closer inspection, aren’t there?”
You’re talking about Earth’s creatures, aren’t you?
“Exactly. But that fact won’t be confirmed until after the problem is solved.”
“So, can Lord Dragon, the representative of the Shieldfreeden, tell the difference between a Raccoon and a Lafu?”
“Of course. After all, the difference between a Lafu and a Raccoon is that Gaelion’s eyes make the tail look striped. Humans apparently can’t tell the difference, but a Lafu doesn’t have stripes.”

“……Huh? Raph…… Judging by Gaelion-chan’s appearance, it sounds kind of like a cross between a tanuki and a raccoon……? Based on that logic, I get the feeling that lesser panda Demi-Humans might also be classified as part of the raccoon species.”

It does seem like they look similar, at least on the surface. I feel like I’ve seen something like that in kids’ anime, too. I remember a character who was called a tanuki but had a striped tail. So that wasn’t the same thing, was it?
“To summarize, it seems there are three types: the girl who was my right-hand woman in the first world, the Raccoon species, and this Raccoon species we’re dealing with now?”
“That’s right. The latter two are a bit hard to tell apart, but you’ll learn to distinguish them by their facial features and personalities.”
I can tell the different types of Filolial-sama, so I get it. I used to be able to tell foreign pigs apart too, but I’m not so sure about that anymore.
“Shouldn’t we recruit that girl who was my right-hand person?”
“Ah… Naofumi, I’d really prefer if you didn’t ask Gaelion to explain that. It’s not that Gaelion is prejudiced, but based on what we know from the loops so far… it’s a bit tricky.”
Rival hedged his words. Well, it’s true that meeting my Older Sister in this loop would be difficult. If we could go back even further in time, it would be certain, but…
“Can’t we save her?”
Father, having sensed the situation, asked with concern.
“It’s too late. By the time the Spear Hero arrived in this loop, we didn’t know her whereabouts, and by the time he returned, it would already be too late. It’s not the Spear Hero’s fault, you know.”

W-what……? It’s creepy that Rival is defending me for some reason! I do think it’s probably too late to save Big Sister in this loop, but there’s no reason for you to take my side. What on earth are you up to!?
“I see…”
“But there are some people I’ve already managed to save in this loop.”
“Oh, really?”
“In the world where Gaelion and Naofumi first met, the female knight there died in prison.”
That did happen, didn’t it? When we returned from Cal Mira Island, there was a grand funeral being held. That should have been the world right after this loop.
“Me?”
“Huh? Does Éclair-san die if she doesn’t meet the conditions?”
Hmm, I’m not so sure. Since she’s safe in the first world, it actually seems more unusual for her to die.
“Éclair, just as Father advised in this loop, the only reason she died was because she got too close to the first world.”
“Iwatani!?”
“Wait a second! That’s not what I meant! Please don’t phrase it in a way that could be misunderstood!”
Oh? Did I phrase that wrong? Still, Éclair is alive in every world except that one. In other words, the problem must lie with Éclair’s resilience.
“Éclair, it’s your fault for being so weak that you die just from being tortured for so long.”
“Well, wouldn’t you die if you were tortured for that long?”
“It’s your fault for not breaking out of prison.”
“You rephrased that… um, is it something like, ‘If I rescue Ms. Eclair, she won’t agree to stay in Melromarc,’ or something like that?”
“That’s right. I left him alone in the first world because he was alive, but he ended up dying.”
The mood has turned rather gloomy. I’d better lighten things up a bit.
“According to Father’s analysis of the next loop, it seems the cause was doing too many good deeds. Éclair, don’t worry—I took you with me in the world after that.”
“That doesn’t exactly put my mind at ease, though… No, right now, my misfortune in another world doesn’t really matter.”
Éclair looked like she wanted to say something, but she seemed to accept it.
“So, I think it’s best not to take ‘Wild Ofumi’ as too much of a role model.”
“Yeah… I know, but if I can help, I want to…”

“The others’ livelihoods are surely guaranteed thanks to the Queen and others’ efforts. I’ve seen in previous loops that they’re capable enough to handle that much. Gaelion will offer some advice, too. You can rest assured that Ofumi in this loop will protect the world. That should also be the wish of the companions in Wild Ofumi’s world.”
Rival said this as if to cheer up her dejected Father. Then, Rival turned her attention to the councilor who had championed the dragon.
“Did you make sure to prove beyond a doubt that supplies were distributed fairly to the surrounding areas, and use that to your advantage?”
“Yes.”
“Then, next comes the starvation tactic. When they go out to plunder neighboring settlements and towns, you’ll suppress them, establish a solid justification, enslave them, and issue forced orders.”

Rival then explained the plan in detail. First, plant bio-plant seeds evenly throughout the surrounding areas to provide food supplies. Based on this, the people of the region would be instructed to maintain public order and ensure the safety of their daily lives, and to work diligently. If anyone failed to comply and attempted to raid other settlements, they would be caught in the act, arrested, enslaved as a serious criminal, and forced to perform various tasks. After all, criminals must be punished appropriately.
“They’ll definitely try to elicit sympathy by using children as a ploy. They’re scoundrels who use starving children as a shield, even though they’re well-fed themselves.”
“You mean if they get caught, they’ll try to escape punishment by using the children as an excuse? That’s…”
“It’s a common ploy used by those struggling in poverty… but given the prior information that they’ve already sold that plant as firewood…”
I can only say they’ve brought this upon themselves. They’re a hopeless bunch. And to think they’re pretending to be relatives of Big Sister… Wouldn’t it be best to dispose of them immediately?
“If even Takt, that miser, can’t handle them… that’s terrifying.”

They’re a tough bunch in more ways than one. …Come to think of it, I seem to recall hearing from the villagers that when Father was developing the village, some people showed up claiming to be relatives of Big Sister, only to be gently turned away by your Older Sister. I heard that a very small number of serious-minded people moved to the neighboring town ruled by my Finacée… Could it be that they came here after hearing about Father’s great achievements?

“If I recall correctly, according to that ‘Wild Ofumi’ story, she said they were a completely different level of evil compared to the people from Melromarc’s neighboring country who were struggling to find food during a famine.”
Ah, come to think of it, I heard that story too. Not only was it a play performed by Keel or someone like that, but it also came up in the next loop of this world.
“Those are the people who snuck into Melromarc trying to get food through barter, aren’t they? That approach is certainly more sensible.”

“They cut down their own food sources, then go and steal when they’re in a bind, and if they get caught, they use their children as a shield to escape punishment… They really can’t be compared to people who sneak in to buy food through barter…”
“Well, I suppose they’re bad, but…” Father is feeling sympathetic. Father is racking his brains over this.

“So, we must prioritize the children’s lives by protecting them from abuse, while simultaneously separating them from their foolish parents to prioritize their education. If they refuse to listen, return them to where they came from on bail; if they commit the same crimes as their parents, impose the same punishment and order them to work diligently.”
I hear the bonds of the slave mark are quite grueling. I suppose that means slackers can’t defy it. But if they slack off even then… death awaits them.
“Children become parents, bear children, enslave them, and devour aid supplies without working a day in their lives. It’s time to break this vicious cycle.”
“As you command… This wouldn’t have been possible if Shieldfreeden hadn’t been defeated by Siltvelt. After all, slavery used to be prohibited in this country.”

Ah, so Shieldfreeden had abolished slavery—at least in name, right? Since they lost the war and became a vassal state, Siltvelt’s laws now apply, I suppose. It’s all about how you go about things, isn’t it?
“Wait—is that what I did in the first world?”

“Wild Ofumi did have some concerns about matters other than Raph, but she didn’t get directly involved. It was the royal family of Melromarc, who had been entrusted with authority by Naofumi, who got involved. Since they were entrusted with governing the world, it couldn’t be helped.”
“Melromarc, you say…”
Éclair seems rather dumbfounded. Is there something odd about Melromarc doing that? Since they’re running a nation, I don’t think it’s strange for them to go that far.
“It’s become quite a chaotic world—one we could never have imagined.”
“It doesn’t sound like a very good story, though…”

“Well, at least this has resolved the issues in Wild Ofumi’s world. If you don’t let the pus drain out, the wound will never heal. This is a difficult problem that must be tackled, even if it means resorting to harsh measures.”
“It sounds like you’re just looking for an excuse to justify it…”
Politics and all that—it’s such a hassle. I hate it. If everyone just came to see the concert, their hearts would surely be united, you know.

“There’s nothing we can do about people starving after cutting down their own bio-plants, so as for those who shield the barbarians raiding other settlements, we’ll just send those barbarians their way. If you’re going to criticize us, then take care of them yourself.”
“Well… by my world’s standards, this logic seems completely flawed, but I guess this is how things work in this world…”
“After that, Gaelion, Naofumi, and the Spear Hero will pretty much wrap things up by playing the victim and preaching justice.”

And just like that, the intractable problems in the troubled region were resolved exactly as Rival had ordered. But man, these guys are something else. Apparently, on the third day after Rival gave the order, they started raiding a nearby settlement.

It seems the people involved had deep-rooted connections, but since the Takt faction had disappeared, they were already a bit unstable, so we managed to successfully root them out—or so the story goes? I’m not really sure what Rival actually did. From what I’ve heard, the people who were secretly pulling the strings behind the scenes to aid the problematic raccoon species were hit by a series of misfortunes, like monster attacks and other disasters happening around them.

However, for a while, there were ongoing issues—including poisoned meals during diplomatic meetings in Shieldfreeden, where I was present, and explosives planted by people not affiliated with the Takt faction. Rival claimed these were people trying to eliminate him because he was a nuisance, but even that died down after a while. Rival had been tracking down and meeting with monster merchants in the Shieldfreeden area—I wonder if there’s some connection there?
As it turned out, I’ve been hearing that since Rival took office, public safety and financial resources in Shieldfreeden have gradually improved—a situation that has become increasingly infuriating.
